podcast.body: This song became Roxy Music's biggest hit in the United States, reaching the Top 40 in 1975. Described as "ahead of its time," it was believed it "would have been a monster smash 10 years later." Its bass line bears a resemblance to Chic's "Good Times," which in turn influenced Sugar Hill Gang's "Rapper's Delight," thereby linking Roxy Music to the origins of both 80s new wave and hip hop/rap. "Love is the drug and I need to score."
